book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.certifica: Numerals carry certificates. The Test Bench certifies a numeral by witness search: 12 is Even because 12 = 6 + 6. Bigger numbers cost more energy.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.circuit_b: The four numerals must be certified Even (Test Bench, or a theorem card).
Four certified even numerals with copper and redstone make a
Four certified even numerals with copper and redstone make a Circuit Board. Boards unlock the reasoning machines.
Variable blocks (paper and lapis) stand for any number; use
Variable blocks (paper and lapis) stand for any number; use one in the air to change its letter. The Drafting Chamber's Assemble mode builds circuits: pick a function, add inputs.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.definitio: Define mode: rename a circuit in an anvil, say Double, to de
Define mode: rename a circuit in an anvil, say Double, to define it. For recursion give a base case, a step using the loop sign (the call one step down), and the variable recursed on.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.first_num: The Zero Source makes 0. The Successor adds one S. A hopper loop counts up. The Duplicator copies a numeral; in the unary age a copy costs its value.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.first_pro: Even(Double(n)): state it on the Property Bench, then give t
Even(Double(n)): state it on the Property Bench, then give the Witness Bench the witness n and Double(n) = n + n. Every Double output can now be certified for free.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.name: Getting Started
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.power.des: Craft a Coal Dynamo (copper, furnace, redstone) and Copper C
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.power.tex: Craft a Coal Dynamo (copper, furnace, redstone) and Copper Cables (3 copper make 8). Machines touching the dynamo or its cables get energy. One coal gives 16,000 units.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.statement: The Equation Bench makes left = right; the same circuit twic
The Equation Bench makes left = right; the same circuit twice gives the proven t = t. The Property Bench makes P(circuit), and its Mode button builds and, implies, not and exists.
book.axiomatic.notebook.basics.the_mathe: Everything here is built from Peano's axioms
Everything here is built from Peano's axioms. Coal pays for energy; mathematics decides how wisely it is spent.
book.axiomatic.notebook.description: Chapters open as you prove things.
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.couriers: If every cable touches an even number of other cables (a loo

If every cable touches an even number of other cables (a loop with no loose ends), an Euler circuit walks each cable once. The Surveyor certifies it, and a Courier Station there delivers its items to every machine in turn.
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.factorie: The Statement Conveyor moves statements and circuits between
The scroll is a proven statement: ∀n. 0 + n = n (zero\_add).
The Statement Conveyor moves statements and circuits between machines; it needs a proven 0 + n = n to craft. The Duplicator copies statements for 1 unit. Every step still costs energy.
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.name: Factories and Networks
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.networks: Cables lose 2% per block of cable
Cables lose 2% per block of cable. A Network Surveyor turns your cables into a graph: if it is a tree, with one route to every machine, it is certified and transfer becomes lossless.
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.phases.d: Click a cable to switch its phase (A copper, B silver)
book.axiomatic.notebook.factory.phases.t: Click a cable to switch its phase (A copper, B silver). If neighbouring cables always differ, the Surveyor certifies alternating power: double speed. Mixed phases without that proof short out, so survey from next to the dynamo.
The Certificate Sorter splits a stream of numerals by a prop
The Certificate Sorter splits a stream of numerals by a property in its filter slot, like Even(n): certified ones drop out below into a hopper, the rest are pushed out the sides.
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.assumption: The Assumption Chamber assumes a statement and stamps what f
The Assumption Chamber assumes a statement and stamps what follows; its variables are locked. Put a conclusion in the discharge slot to get H -> Q.
The Induction Engine takes P(0), the step P(n) -> P(S(n)) an
The Induction Engine takes P(0), the step P(n) -> P(S(n)) and the variable n, and proves P(n) for every n. Start with 0 + n = n: six machine steps.
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.name: Logic and Proof
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.opening_ex: Put a proven exists, like exists j
Put a proven exists, like exists j. a = j + j, in a chamber with a Variable in its open-as slot: you get a = j + j to work with. Close it by discharging a conclusion that does not mention j.
Instantiator: put a circuit in for a variable

Instantiator: put a circuit in for a variable. Rewriter: swap one side of a proven equation for the other; its variables match anything. Conjunction and Modus Ponens Presses: and, and P -> Q with P gives Q.
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.speed_card: A proven a + b = b + a in the Compiled Machine's card slot i
A proven a + b = b + a in the Compiled Machine's card slot is a speed card: the machine swaps its inputs to recurse on the smaller one. Only fully proven symmetries work.
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.the_librar: Name mode: rename a proven statement in an anvil to file it
Name mode: rename a proven statement in an anvil to file it as a theorem. The Library block lists definitions, theorems, conjectures and tests. The Graph Lens shows any object's graph.
book.axiomatic.notebook.logic.theorem_ca: The Compiled Machine runs a defined function on numerals
The Compiled Machine runs a defined function on numerals. A proven statement about it in the card slot certifies each output for 1 unit: no more searching.
book.axiomatic.notebook.name: The Mathematician's Notebook
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.general_r: Euclid's algorithm calls itself on smaller numbers, not just

Euclid's algorithm calls itself on smaller numbers, not just one step down. Give the Drafting Chamber the body, a measure and a proof that the measure shrinks at each call. Define ifz(t, e, c) by recursion on c to branch.
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.infinitel: Prove that above every n there is a prime: for all n, exists
The scroll is a proven statement: ∀n. ∃p. n ≤ p ∧ Prime(p), that primes never run out.

Prove that above every n there is a prime: for all n, exists p, n <= p and Prime(p). That proof crafts the Infinite Prime Well, which emits primes forever. The Factorization Vault stores items as one number.
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.name: The Prime Path
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.perfect_n: A Mersenne prime is a prime one less than a power of two, li
The numeral must be certified both Prime and Mersenne, by proof or computation: no conjectures.

A Mersenne prime is a prime one less than a power of two, like 7 or 31. By Euclid and Euler each one gives a perfect number. A Perfect Core needs a numeral certified both Prime and Mersenne, without conjectures.
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.prime_cor: Prime is predefined: 2 <= n and no d with 2 <= d < n divides
The four numerals must be certified Prime.
Prime is predefined: 2 <= n and no d with 2 <= d < n divides n. The Test Bench can certify primes by trying every d: slow and costly. Cards and deciders make it cheap.
book.axiomatic.notebook.primes.prime_for: The Forge finds the next prime from a candidate, certified b
The Forge finds the next prime from a candidate, certified by its method card H(n) -> Prime(n). A proven decider link is safe. A conjectured test is fast, until a Carmichael number like 561 comes by.
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.conjectures: The Conjecture Bench turns a named claim into a card and a b
The Conjecture Bench turns a named claim into a card and a block. Keep the block powered. Each use is checked: one counterexample and it fails, with everything built on it.
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.deciders.de: A decider is a circuit answering 1 or 0, like isPrime
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.deciders.te: A decider is a circuit answering 1 or 0, like isPrime. Prove both links, f(n) = 1 -> P(n) and P(n) -> f(n) = 1, and link them in the Drafting Chamber: then machines compute P with f.
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.name: Testing and Risk
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.safety.desc: An unpowered conjecture block goes dormant: safe, but its ca
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.safety.name: Safety
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.safety.text: An unpowered conjecture block goes dormant: safe, but its cards stop working. Seal a conjecture block in obsidian or tinted glass near a Containment Controller to keep its failure harmless.
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.testing.des: Put a statement and a bound numeral in the Test Bench: it ch
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.testing.tex: Put a statement and a bound numeral in the Test Bench: it checks every case up to the bound. Tested statements work as cards inside their range. One counterexample refutes forever.
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.traps.descr: Famous false claims: 2n + 1 is always prime
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.traps.name: Traps
book.axiomatic.notebook.risk.traps.text: Famous false claims: 2n + 1 is always prime. n*n + n + 41 is always prime. a + b is a valid pairing. Test before you trust. A proof is forever.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.arith: Define a ≡ b mod 5 as ∃j ∃k. a + j×5 = b + k×5. Prove it reflexive, symmetric and transitive (distributivity helps), certify it, and name a law that it respects +. The Rewriter then drops multiples of 5 inside sums.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.binar: Prove every number is halves plus a bit: n = (h(n) + h(n)) +

Prove every number is halves plus a bit: n = (h(n) + h(n)) + p(n) and p(n) ≤ 1. Name it in the Library and numbers go binary: + and × and the Duplicator pay per digit, not per unit. Hint: par flips, half adds par.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.equiv: Certify a relation as an Equivalence in the Structure Bench

Certify a relation as an Equivalence in the Structure Bench and the Rewriter accepts s ≡ t in place of an equation. It rewrites only inside functions that respect ≡: name a law like a ≡ b → c ≡ d → a + c ≡ b + d in the Library for each one.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.faste: Prove fast(x) = slow(x) and put the proof in the Implementat
Prove fast(x) = slow(x) and put the proof in the Implementation Bench: every machine computes slow with fast from then on, and every theorem about slow still holds.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.monoi: SetMonoid is a monoid on a set A: e is in A, A is closed, an
SetMonoid is a monoid on a set A: e is in A, A is closed, and each law assumes its inputs are in A. Multiplication mod n needs it, since 1 is its identity only below n.
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.name: Structures and Speed
book.axiomatic.notebook.structures.struc: The Structure Bench shows the axioms of monoids, equivalence
The Structure Bench shows the axioms of monoids, equivalences and orders. Prove a theorem once for any monoid, certify an operation's three laws, and apply the theorem to it for free.
book.axiomatic.notebook.tooltip: Mathematics from Peano's axioms, one machine at a time
